text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday.
- Many Serbs from Eastern Slavonia are looting Croatian property and transporting it, together with their own belongings, across the border to Yugoslavia.

- Foreign Minister Mate Granic says Croatia could sign an agreement on cooperation with European Union in the second half of this year. Also, the country will meet all conditions for entering CEFTA by the end of 1997 and should join the WTO in January 1998.

- Opposition politician Stipe Mesic testified against Croatia and President Franjo Tudjman before the U.N. war crimes tribunal in The Hague. Mesic was the last president of the collective Presidency of socialist Yugoslavia and one of the founders of the Croatian ruling party HDZ.
- The first group of some 40 Croatian refugee families will return to Eastern Slavonia next week.
- The presidential election is getting closer but the opposition still has no candidate and its chances of choosing one are getting smaller.
- The harmonious coexistance of Croats and returning Serbs in the former Krajina region is not likely as mistrust reigns.
- Munich tourism fair representatives visit Croatia to consider its candidacy as co-host for next year's exhibition. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
